newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Banerj official sees sale in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Banerj official sees sale in Dec.

text.p: Banerj, the first Brazilian state bank to be privatized, will go on sale next month as soon as the bank's majority shareholder and the federal government settle their accounts with the bank, an official said.

Rio de Janeiro state and the federal government are expected to reach an accord on debt owed to Banerj by late November, said Paulo Ferraz, president of private bank Bozano Simonsen, which was hired to manage Banerj and prepare it for privatization.

"We expect an agreement between the state and federal government by the end of this month," he said, adding that the tender specifications would be published 15 days later, allowing the auction to take place in mid-December.
Bozano Simonsen was awarded a contract last January to run Banerj, replacing the Central Bank which had taken over Banerj in December 1994.
The negotiations are aimed at finding ways to refinance Rio de Janeiro's 500 million real debt with Banerj under the terms of a decree designed for the restructuring of state banks.
Under the decree, the federal government would provide 100 percent of financing needed to restructure debt owed to banks being privatized, liquidated or turned into development banks.

According to Banerj's privatization plan, what will be sold to investors will be the healthy portion of the bank. That portion, with a 180 million real net worth, was created through a capital injection to Banerj's brokerage arm, allowing it to be transformed into a retail bank.
The capitalization was effected by transferring the bank's viable assets to the brokerage arm.
This bit of financial engineering allowed the separation of the bank from its bad loans, which are the subject of talks between the state and federal government and will remain with the state.
Ferraz said the auction particulars have not been nailed down yet, but he added that Banerj bank and Banerj Seguros, its insurance subsidiary, would both be sold on the same day.

Bozano is also negotiating with the Central Bank and the state government on when Banerj's minimum price will be announced, he added. Ferraz said he prefers to announce the price 48 hours ahead of the auction.

Seven financial institutions have prequalified to bid on Banerj at auction. They are Brazil's Bradesco, Banco Itau and Companhia de Investimentos Latino Americana, Banco BBA Creditanstalt, Bank of Boston Brazil unit, France's CCF and GE Capital Corp.
The same seven institutions, plus health insurance firm Golden Cross, also prequalified for the privatization of Banerj Seguros.
Ferraz said he was not surprised that Banerj's sale has drawn foreign institutions as well as major Brazilian retail banks.
"For us, it's a not surprise. Once the adjustments were made, we knew that Banerj was the type of bank which would attract interest," he said.
BBA, one of the banks that prequalified, said it was interested in Banerj because it wants to enter retail banking.

"We have always been a wholesale bank and we understood that the retail segment was interesting to us under our plans for expansion," said Fernao Bracher, president of BBA. "Banerj is located in an important region and has an interesting number of branches."
